knowledge:
- key_parameters: data=Matrix or data frame containing expression data where rows are features and columns are samples ;; cl=Vector of class labels (0 and 1 for two-class, or all 1s for one-class/paired/ratio data) ;; origin=Vector of origin labels (1 to L) indicating the source laboratory or batch for multi-origin datasets ;; logged=Logical indicating if the input data is already log-transformed (default is TRUE) ;; gene.names=Vector of gene or feature names to be displayed in the output ;; plot=Logical to control the graphical display of estimated pfp vs. number of identified genes ;; rand=Integer setting the random seed for reproducible permutation/pairing results ;; calculateProduct=Logical; if TRUE (default), performs Rank Product (RP) analysis; if FALSE, performs Rank Sum (RS) analysis ;; cutoff=The pfp or p-value threshold used to select significant features ;; method=Selection criterion in topGene, either "pfp" (percentage of false prediction, default) or "pval" (p-value) ;; num.gene=The number of top genes to identify if cutoff is not specified
- alternatives: SAM (from siggenes package)=Mentioned as having identical input arguments (data and cl) for two-class analysis ;; limma=Mentioned as an alternative for cDNA arrays that explicitly handles complex designs like dye swaps, whereas RankProd simplifies these designs ;; vsn=Mentioned and used for variance stabilization and normalization of cDNA and metabolomics data prior to RankProd analysis
- when_to_use: Use when identifying differentially expressed genes or metabolites across replicated experiments under weak assumptions (e.g., only a minority of features change, measurements are independent, and variance is roughly equal) ;; Use when combining datasets from different origins (e.g., different laboratories or drug dosages) where raw values are not directly comparable ;; Use when looking for features with consistent up- or down-regulation, or complex rank-based patterns (e.g., up in one condition and down in another)
- pitfalls: Inputting non-log-transformed data without setting logged=FALSE ;; Failing to apply variance stabilization (like vsn) to metabolomics data where the equal variance assumption is violated ;; Calling topGene without specifying either cutoff or num.gene, which results in an error ;; Relying on the old unpaired procedure which had a higher False Discovery Rate (the package now defaults to a more principled random pairing approach)

workflows.name: single_origin_analysis
workflows.intent: Identify differentially expressed genes from a single-origin dataset using the Rank Product method.
input: class_labels.txt (Vector of class labels, e.g., 0 for control and 1 for treatment)
workflows.stages: 1. Run RankProducts to perform the Rank Product analysis ;; 2. Plot the estimated pfp vs. number of identified genes using plotRP ;; 3. Extract significant up- and down-regulated genes using topGene.
workflows.code:
RP.out <- RankProducts(arab.sub,arab.cl.sub, logged=TRUE,
na.rm=FALSE,plot=FALSE,  rand=123)
plotRP(RP.out, cutoff=0.05)
topGene(RP.out,cutoff=0.05,method="pfp",
logged=TRUE,logbase=2,gene.names=arab.gnames)

workflows.name: multi_origin_analysis
workflows.intent: Combine datasets from multiple laboratories or origins to perform an overall differential expression analysis.
input: class_labels.txt (Vector of class labels across all samples)
origin_labels.txt (Vector of origin labels indicating sample source)
workflows.stages: 1. Run RP.advance to perform multi-origin Rank Product analysis ;; 2. Plot the estimated pfp vs. number of identified genes using plotRP ;; 3. Extract significant genes across all origins using topGene.

workflows.name: cdna_common_reference
workflows.intent: Identify differentially expressed genes from cDNA microarray data using a common reference design.
input: cdna_intensities.tsv (Matrix containing red and green intensities for reference and sample channels)
workflows.stages: 1. Normalize intensities (e.g., using vsn) ;; 2. Calculate log-ratios by subtracting reference intensities from sample intensities ;; 3. Run RankProducts on the log-ratios with class labels ;; 4. Extract significant genes using topGene.
workflows.code:
refrs <- (1:8)*2-1
samps <- (1:8)*2
M <- lym.exp[,samps]-lym.exp[,refrs]
cl <- c(rep(0,4),rep(1,4))
RP.out <- RankProducts(M,cl, logged=TRUE, rand=123)
topGene(RP.out,cutoff=0.05,logged=TRUE,logbase=exp(1))

workflows.name: metabolomics_rank_sum
workflows.intent: Identify differentially expressed metabolites from LC/MS data using the Rank Sum method.
input: metabolite_intensity_matrix.tsv (Basepeak intensity matrix of identified metabolites)
class_labels.txt (Vector of class labels for spiked/control samples)
workflows.stages: 1. Normalize and stabilize variance of the intensity matrix (e.g., using vsn) ;; 2. Run RankProducts with calculateProduct=FALSE to perform Rank Sum analysis ;; 3. Extract significant metabolites using topGene.
workflows.code:
RS.apples<-RankProducts(apples.data.vsn, apples.cl,
                        gene.names = rownames(apples.data.vsn), 
                        calculateProduct = FALSE, rand=123)
topGene(RS.apples,cutoff = 0.05, method = "pfp",
        gene.names = rownames(apples.data.vsn))
selected <- which(RS.apples$pfp[,1]<= 0.05)

workflows.name: multi_condition_contrast
workflows.intent: Simultaneously identify genes up-regulated under one condition and down-regulated under another by switching class labels.
workflows.stages: 1. Modify class labels for one of the origins to invert the comparison direction ;; 2. Run RP.advance with calculateProduct=FALSE to perform Rank Sum analysis ;; 3. Extract significant genes using topGene ;; 4. Plot the results using plotRP.
workflows.code:
arab.cl2 <- arab.cl
arab.cl2[arab.cl==0 &arab.origin==2] <- 1
arab.cl2[arab.cl==1 &arab.origin==2] <- 0
Rsum.adv.out <- RP.advance(arab,arab.cl2,arab.origin,calculateProduct=FALSE,
logged=TRUE,gene.names=arab.gnames,rand=123)
topGene(Rsum.adv.out,cutoff=0.05,gene.names=arab.gnames)
plotRP(Rsum.adv.out,cutoff=0.05)
